headline: High: agentic-flow can write/egress and modify git while opik has broad network egress, creating default-risk leakage and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content; agent_b exposes a REST API and broad egress, so outputs can be bridged through shared workflows. No shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred rather than direct.
conditions: IF agent_a reads agent_b output from stdin/stdout or MCP without provenance checks
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the agents
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted text
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require explicit allowlists for prompt-bearing fields
Run the pair in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before any agent-to-agent handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and can egress over allowlisted network; agent_b has broad network egress. Even without a documented shared filesystem, any handoff of those data classes to agent_b could leak sensitive repository context through its API calls.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards repository metadata or task prompts to agent_b
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or ticket stream
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to redacted inputs only
Separate workspaces and credentials
Block outbound calls from agent_b for sensitive runs
Review logs for prompt or code exfiltration
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b has broad network egress and REST API access. If both are attached to the same mutable repo or shared state, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt work or history.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF agent_b writes back into a shared mutable resource via its API
mitigations: Serialize access to the repository
Use per-agent branches or clones
Disable git writes for one agent during joint runs
Add a lock file around mutable operations
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate and transform content via shell/MCP workflows, and agent_b exposes a REST API that may consume upstream outputs. If agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports; verification is not documented.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a output without validation
IF agent_a's generated artifacts are used as inputs to agent_b evaluation or publishing
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on all handoffs
Compare outputs against source artifacts
Limit agent_b to read-only evaluation mode
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and unverified, but only agent_a explicitly handles Ed25519 signatures and repository metadata; agent_b lists no sensitive data classes or residency constraints. The pair shows no direct residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited and mostly documentation gaps.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_a's repository workflows
IF deployment policy requires documented residency or retention controls
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Avoid placing regulated data in shared repos
Review retention settings before deployment
Tag signature material as sensitive
requires-engineering: add compliance controls to the orchestrator
